raw_case_text:
This is a fifty-one year old female patient with history of diabetes mellitus and systemic lupus erythematoses (SLE) complicated by lupus nephritis. Although we have included her case in our previous publication, we have not reported her clinical details at that time. She was put on prednisolone 30 mg and azathioprine 100 mg daily since end of June and mid-July 2002, respectively. She was admitted to Queen Mary Hospital on 11th August 2002 for investigation of jaundice. Investigations revealed deranged liver function tests with cholestatic pattern. A diagnosis of drug-induced hepatotoxicity was entertained, and azathioprine was stopped after admission. As her autoimmune disease was under control, her steroid dosage was reduced from 25 mg to 15 mg daily within the next 14 days. Her CXR taken on admission was normal.
Soon after her immunosuppressive therapy was tapered, she developed fever and non-productive cough. A repeat CXR performed on 9th Sept revealed new infiltrate over the left mid-zone, suggestive of pneumonia. She was started on intravenous ceftazidime 1 gram eight hourly and oral clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily. Serial CXR performed three days later showed increasing bilateral pulmonary infiltrates and worsening hypoxemia. There was an upsurge of total lymphocyte count from 0.7 x 109/L (total white cell count 7.2 x 109/L) at the time of admission to 5.6 x 109/L (total white cell count 10.8 x 109/L) at the time of clinical deterioration. Bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy performed on the same day revealed Pneumocystitis jiroveci by methenamine sliver stain. Workup for other opportunistic pathogens including cytomegalovirus and aspergillus was negative. She was commenced on intravenous pentamidine (4 mg/kg/day) and corticosteroids for severe PCP infection. Despite active treatment she developed progressive respiratory failure and required admission to intensive care unit. She subsequently recovered after a stormy hospital course, and upon discharge from hospital, her total lymphocyte count had returned to her baseline of 0.86 x 109/L.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 51-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, lupus nephritis, and diabetes mellitus developed acute fever and nonproductive cough shortly after stopping azathioprine and tapering prednisolone for drug-induced cholestatic jaundice.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient had been started on oral prednisolone (30 mg daily at the end of June 2002) and azathioprine (100 mg daily in mid-July 2002) for SLE and lupus nephritis. On August 11, 2002, she was admitted to Queen Mary Hospital for cholestatic jaundice attributed to azathioprine hepatotoxicity; admission chest X-ray was normal, azathioprine was discontinued, and her prednisolone dose was tapered from 25 mg to 15 mg daily over 14 days. Shortly after this rapid tapering of immunosuppression (early September 2002), she developed acute fever and a nonproductive cough.
subjective.past_medical_history: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) complicated by lupus nephritis; diabetes mellitus; azathioprine-induced cholestatic hepatotoxicity (August 2002).
subjective.review_of_systems: Initial admission positive for jaundice; September 2002 inpatient course positive for fever, nonproductive cough, and progressive hypoxemic dyspnea. Recent medications were prednisolone (tapered from 30 mg to 15 mg daily) and azathioprine (100 mg daily, stopped on admission).

objective.physical_examination: Initial admission notable for clinical jaundice; subsequent September 2002 deterioration marked by fever and progressive hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring ICU admission.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission liver profile: Cholestatic liver function test derangement. Serial leukocyte and lymphocyte counts: Admission WBC 7.2 x 10^9/L with baseline lymphopenia (total lymphocyte count 0.7 x 10^9/L), which surged sharply to a total lymphocyte count of 5.6 x 10^9/L (WBC 10.8 x 10^9/L) during acute PCP clinical deterioration before returning to 0.86 x 10^9/L at hospital discharge. Serial chest radiographs: Normal on August 11 admission; new left mid-zone infiltrate on September 9; rapidly progressive bilateral pulmonary infiltrates 3 days later.
objective.advanced_workup: Bronchoscopy with transbronchial lung biopsy (September 12, 2002): Methenamine silver staining of transbronchial biopsy specimen identified Pneumocystis jirovecii; workup for cytomegalovirus (CMV), Aspergillus, and other opportunistic pathogens was negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Severe Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP; confirmed by methenamine silver staining on transbronchial lung biopsy) precipitated by immune reconstitution (marked by an 8-fold surge in peripheral lymphocytes from 0.7 to 5.6 x 10^9/L) following azathioprine withdrawal and rapid corticosteroid tapering in a patient with SLE and lupus nephritis. Plan and clinical course: After failing initial empiric IV ceftazidime (1 g q8h) and oral clarithromycin (500 mg BID), she was treated with intravenous pentamidine (4 mg/kg/day), systemic corticosteroids, and ICU supportive care for progressive respiratory failure, ultimately achieving full clinical recovery and discharge.
